def set_paths(h):
    """main() calls this after resolving the portable home directory."""
    global HOME, CONFIG_PATH, JOBS_PATH
    HOME = h
    CONFIG_PATH = HOME / "settings.json"
    JOBS_PATH = HOME / "jobs.json"


def portable_home():
    """If portable.txt sits next to the executable, keep settings/jobs with it."""
    if getattr(sys, "frozen", False):
        base = Path(sys.executable).parent
    else:
        base = Path(__file__).parent
    if (base / "portable.txt").exists():
        STATE["portable"] = True
        return base / "VideoGrabberData"
    return HOME



def load_settings():
    if CONFIG_PATH.exists():
        try:
            STATE.update(json.loads(CONFIG_PATH.read_text()))
        except Exception as e:
            log(f"couldn't read settings.json ({e}); using defaults")
    _migrate_settings(STATE)
    if not STATE.get("api_token"):
        STATE["api_token"] = secrets.token_hex(16)
        save_settings()


def save_settings():
    HOME.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    tmp = CONFIG_PATH.with_suffix(".json.tmp")
    tmp.write_text(json.dumps(STATE, indent=2))
    os.replace(tmp, CONFIG_PATH)



ILLEGAL_FILENAME_CHARS_RE = re.compile(r'[<>:"/\\|?*\x00-\x1f]')


# Windows device names: a file called CON, NUL.txt or com1.tar.gz cannot be
# created (or opened) on NTFS, with or without an extension.
_WIN_RESERVED_NAMES = frozenset(
    ["CON", "PRN", "AUX", "NUL"]
    + [f"COM{i}" for i in range(1, 10)]
    + [f"LPT{i}" for i in range(1, 10)])


def safe_filename(name):
    """Strip Windows-illegal characters, collapse whitespace, trim trailing
    dots/spaces, and cap the length so the resulting file can be created.
    Reserved device names (CON, PRN, AUX, NUL, COM1-9, LPT1-9) get a "_"
    prefix; the extension is preserved."""
    name = ILLEGAL_FILENAME_CHARS_RE.sub("_", name)
    name = re.sub(r"\s+", " ", name).strip()
    name = name.rstrip(". ")
    if not name:
        name = "download"
    # Windows matches the device name before the FIRST dot, so "con.tar.gz"
    # is reserved too, not just a bare "con".
    if name.split(".", 1)[0].rstrip(" ").upper() in _WIN_RESERVED_NAMES:
        name = "_" + name
    if len(name) > 180:
        stem, ext = os.path.splitext(name)
        name = stem[: 180 - len(ext)] + ext
    return name


# Whole destination paths stay under this many characters (Windows
# MAX_PATH is 260). The reserve leaves room for the suffixes added around
# a file name: ".part7", ".merge", " (12)".
_PATH_BUDGET = 240
_PATH_SUFFIX_RESERVE = 16


def truncate_for_dir(base_dir, category, subdir, name):
    """Shorten `name` so base_dir/category/subdir/name (plus the suffix
    reserve) stays inside _PATH_BUDGET. Keeps the extension. Pass "" for a
    category or subdir that is not part of the path. A name that already
    fits is returned unchanged."""
    try:
        d = Path(base_dir)
        if category:
            d = d / category
        if subdir:
            d = d / subdir
        room = _PATH_BUDGET - _PATH_SUFFIX_RESERVE - len(str(d)) - 1
    except Exception:
        return name
    if len(name) <= room:
        return name
    # A directory this deep is the user's problem; never shrink to nothing.
    room = max(room, 24)
    stem, ext = os.path.splitext(name)
    if len(ext) > 16:
        stem, ext = name, ""
    keep = max(room - len(ext), 8)
    return (stem[:keep].rstrip(". ") or "download") + ext


_CT_EXT_MAP = [
    ("video/mp4", ".mp4"), ("video/webm", ".webm"), ("video/x-matroska", ".mkv"),
    ("video/quicktime", ".mov"), ("video/x-msvideo", ".avi"), ("video/mp2t", ".ts"),
    ("audio/mpeg", ".mp3"), ("audio/mp4", ".m4a"), ("audio/x-m4a", ".m4a"),
    ("audio/wav", ".wav"), ("audio/x-wav", ".wav"), ("audio/flac", ".flac"),
    ("audio/aac", ".aac"), ("audio/ogg", ".ogg"), ("audio/opus", ".opus"),
    ("application/zip", ".zip"),
    ("application/x-zip-compressed", ".zip"), ("application/x-7z-compressed", ".7z"),
    ("application/x-rar-compressed", ".rar"), ("application/pdf", ".pdf"),
    ("application/epub+zip", ".epub"), ("application/x-mobipocket-ebook", ".mobi"),
    ("application/json", ".json"), ("text/markdown", ".md"),
    ("application/x-tar", ".tar"), ("application/gzip", ".gz"),
    ("application/x-bzip2", ".bz2"), ("application/x-xz", ".xz"),
    ("application/zstd", ".zst"), ("application/x-iso9660-image", ".iso"),
    ("image/jpeg", ".jpg"), ("image/png", ".png"), ("image/gif", ".gif"),
    ("image/webp", ".webp"), ("image/avif", ".avif"), ("image/heic", ".heic"),
    ("image/tiff", ".tiff"), ("image/bmp", ".bmp"), ("image/svg+xml", ".svg"),
    ("font/woff2", ".woff2"), ("font/woff", ".woff"),
    ("application/font-woff", ".woff"), ("application/vnd.ms-fontobject", ".eot"),
]
_HEAD_EXT_CACHE = {}


def guess_ext_from_head(url):
    """HEAD the URL and map Content-Type to an extension. Cached per-URL so
    repeated guesses (restored jobs, retries) don't re-hit the server."""
    if url in _HEAD_EXT_CACHE:
        return _HEAD_EXT_CACHE[url]
    ext = ""
    try:
        r = requests.head(url, allow_redirects=True,
                          timeout=STATE["connection_timeout"])
        ct = (r.headers.get("Content-Type") or "").split(";")[0].strip().lower()
        for mime, e in _CT_EXT_MAP:
            if ct == mime:
                ext = e
                break
        if not ext:
            cd = r.headers.get("Content-Disposition")
            if cd:
                m = re.search(r'filename\*?=(?:UTF-8\'\')?"?([^";]+)"?', cd)
                if m:
                    ext = os.path.splitext(unquote(m.group(1)))[1]
    except Exception:
        pass
    if ext:
        _HEAD_EXT_CACHE[url] = ext
        if len(_HEAD_EXT_CACHE) > 5000:
            _HEAD_EXT_CACHE.clear()
    return ext


_QUERY_NAME_KEYS = ("fn", "filename", "file", "name", "file_name", "path")

# "?format=jpg" / "?f=mp4" style extension hints (pbs.twimg.com and friends).
# Anchored on purpose: "?format=json" must NOT match.
_QUERY_FORMAT_KEYS = ("format", "f")
_QUERY_FORMAT_RE = re.compile(
    r"^(?:jpg|jpeg|png|webp|gif|avif|bmp|svg|tif|tiff|heic|heif|"
    r"mp4|webm|mov|m4v|mkv|mp3|m4a|wav|flac|opus|ogg)$", re.I)


def _filename_from_query(url):
    """Pick a filename out of a query string (fn=, filename=, ...).
    Returns "" when none looks usable."""
    try:
        qs = parse_qs(urlparse(url).query)
    except Exception:
        return ""
    for key in _QUERY_NAME_KEYS:
        for v in qs.get(key, []):
            v = (v or "").strip()
            if not v:
                continue
            if key == "path":
                # "?path=/mnt/user-data/outputs/report.zip" (claude.ai) or a
                # Windows-style path: normalise separators, decode again
                # (the value is often double-encoded), keep the basename.
                base = os.path.basename(unquote(v).replace("\\", "/"))
                if base and os.path.splitext(base)[1] and len(base) < 200:
                    return base
                continue
            # Only accept values that look like a filename with an
            # extension: "report.pdf" yes, "abc123" no, "a/b" no.
            base = os.path.basename(v.replace("\\", "/"))
            if base and os.path.splitext(base)[1] and len(base) < 200:
                return unquote(base)
    # No usable name key: accept "format=jpg" when the URL path itself has
    # no extension (https://pbs.twimg.com/media/ABC?format=jpg&name=large).
    try:
        path_base = unquote(os.path.basename(urlparse(url).path))
    except ValueError:
        path_base = ""
    if path_base and not os.path.splitext(path_base)[1]:
        for v in qs.get("format", []):
            v = (v or "").strip().lower()
            if _QUERY_FORMAT_RE.match(v):
                return safe_filename(f"{path_base}.{v}")
    return ""


def guess_filename(url, content_disposition=None):
    if content_disposition:
        m = re.search(r'filename\*?=(?:UTF-8\'\')?"?([^";]+)"?', content_disposition)
        if m:
            return safe_filename(unquote(m.group(1)))
    qname = _filename_from_query(url)
    if qname:
        return safe_filename(qname)
    try:
        path = urlparse(url).path
    except ValueError:
        path = ""
    name = os.path.basename(path) or "download"
    return safe_filename(unquote(name))


_REDDIT_CDN_HOST_RE = re.compile(r"(^|\.)(v|packaged-media)\.redd\.it$", re.I)


def preferred_stem(job):
    """Title-derived filename stem for Reddit CDN downloads, else None.

    Reddit's CDN names files m2-res_1280p.mp4 / DASH_720.mp4. When the job
    carries the post's page_url (".../comments/<id>/<slug>/"), the slug is a
    better stem. NOTE: jobs do not store page_url yet (new_job only derives
    source_site from it), so this returns None until that field exists.
    Nothing calls it yet."""
    try:
        host = urlparse(job.get("url") or "").hostname or ""
        page = job.get("page_url")
        if not page or not _REDDIT_CDN_HOST_RE.search(host):
            return None
        parts = [p for p in urlparse(page).path.split("/") if p]
        if "comments" in parts:
            i = parts.index("comments")
            if len(parts) > i + 2:
                slug = unquote(parts[i + 2]).replace("_", " ").strip()
                if slug:
                    return safe_filename(slug)
    except Exception:
        pass
    return None


# Only suffixes _unique_path itself would have added: " (2)" to " (999)".
# A year or other real number ("Report (2019).pdf") is part of the name.
_UNIQUE_SUFFIX_RE = re.compile(r"(?: \((?:[2-9]|[1-9]\d{1,2})\))+$")


def _unique_path(path, taken=None):
    """If path exists, append ' (2)', ' (3)', ... before the extension.

    `taken` is an optional collection of lower-cased path strings that count
    as occupied even though no file exists yet (in-flight reservations, see
    downloader._job_dest). Raises RuntimeError after 1000 collisions: the
    old behaviour of returning the existing path made callers overwrite it."""
    def _busy(p):
        return p.exists() or (taken is not None and str(p).lower() in taken)

    if not _busy(path):
        return path
    stem, ext = os.path.splitext(path.name)
    # Collapse existing " (N)" suffixes first so repeats never stack into
    # "name (2) (2).mp4".
    stem = _UNIQUE_SUFFIX_RE.sub("", stem) or stem
    for i in range(2, 1001):
        candidate = path.with_name(f"{stem} ({i}){ext}")
        if not _busy(candidate):
            return candidate
    raise RuntimeError(f"no free file name for {path.name} after 1000 tries")


# v5.5: HLS/DASH playlists are video streams. Their URL basename ends in
# .m3u8 / .mpd, which is in no extension set, so they were created as "Other".
_STREAM_EXT_CATEGORY = {".m3u8": "Video", ".m3u": "Video", ".mpd": "Video"}


def category_for(filename):
    # Batch 5: tolerate query/fragment leftovers and trailing dots/spaces so a
    # name like "clip.mp4?x=1" or "song.mp3 " still lands in the right folder.
    # New jobs only: nothing here relabels existing jobs or moves files.
    filename = re.split(r"[?#]", str(filename or ""), maxsplit=1)[0].rstrip(". ")
    _, ext = split_ext(filename)
    ext = ext.lower()
    return CATEGORY_MAP.get(ext) or _STREAM_EXT_CATEGORY.get(ext, "Other")


# Any URL whose path ends in one of these extensions is a plain file
# fetch, not something yt-dlp should extract. Covers media files the
# user might want, AND arbitrary files (scripts, archives, docs) that
# shouldn't be pushed through yt-dlp's extractor pipeline at all.
# html/htm/php are deliberately NOT listed: a page URL such as
# https://site.com/v/123.html should try yt-dlp first (it is usually a video
# page), not be saved as an HTML file. It is matched against the URL PATH only.
# One tuple drives BOTH the path check and the query-value check below, so
# they can never drift. Covers every family _CATEGORY_EXTS knows about (the
# app is a general download manager) plus code files.
# html/htm/php are deliberately NOT listed: a page URL such as
# https://site.com/v/123.html should try yt-dlp first (it is usually a video
# page), not be saved as an HTML file. It is matched against the URL PATH only.
_PLAIN_FILE_EXTS = (
    "mp4|m4v|mov|webm|mkv|avi|flv|wmv|mpg|mpeg|ts|m2ts|mts|vob|ogv|divx|rm|rmvb|asf|mxf|3gp|3g2|"
    "mp3|wav|flac|m4a|aac|ogg|opus|wma|aiff|aif|alac|ape|m4b|mid|midi|amr|"
    "zip|rar|7z|tar|gz|bz2|xz|lz|lzma|zst|cab|iso|img|tgz|"
    "pdf|docx?|xlsx?|pptx?|txt|md|rtf|csv|tsv|json|xml|yaml|yml|odt|ods|odp|epub|mobi|azw3|"
    "css|"
    "py|js|ts|java|c|cpp|h|hpp|rs|go|rb|sh|bat|cmd|ps1|"
    "exe|msi|dmg|deb|rpm|apk|appimage|appx|jar|"
    "jpg|jpeg|jpe|png|gif|webp|avif|svg|bmp|ico|tif|tiff|heic|heif|jxl|psd|raw|dng|cr2|nef|xcf|"
    "ttf|otf|woff2?|eot"
)
_PLAIN_FILE_EXT_RE = re.compile(r"\.(" + _PLAIN_FILE_EXTS + r")(\?|#|$)", re.I)

# Page extensions: a URL ending in one of these is a document page, not a
# file — yt-dlp gets first crack at it (its generic extractor can still pull
# a player out of the page).
_PAGE_EXT_RE = re.compile(r"\.(html?|php|aspx?|jsp|do)(\?|#|$)", re.I)
# ANY other dotted suffix on the path means "some file", even an extension
# we don't know: the generic engine just copies bytes and names it from the
# URL, while yt-dlp would download it and name the result the infamous
# "UNKNOWN_VIDEO" (an .epub URL used to land that way before .epub was in
# _PLAIN_FILE_EXTS). At least one letter required, so "/v/1.5" is not a file.
_EXT_LIKE_RE = re.compile(r"\.[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9]{0,7}(\?|#|$)")

# Query params that commonly carry the filename (Dropbox, ChatGPT,
# S3 presigned URLs, Google Drive, generic file hosts).
_FILENAME_QUERY_KEYS = ("fn", "filename", "file", "name", "file_name")


def detect_type(url):
    if ".m3u8" in url.lower() or ".mpd" in url.lower():
        return "ytdlp"
    # Path only: an extension-looking string in a query value or host must
    # not route a page URL to the generic downloader (the query-value check
    # below handles fn=/filename=/format= on its own terms).
    try:
        _url_path = urlparse(url).path
    except ValueError:
        _url_path = ""
    if _PLAIN_FILE_EXT_RE.search(_url_path):
        return "generic"
    # Filename in the query string? (fn=..., filename=..., file=...)
    # Match the extension regex against each value; anchor it so
    # "?fn=foo.pdf" matches but "?fn=foo.pdfbar" doesn't.
    try:
        qs = parse_qs(urlparse(url).query)
        for key in _FILENAME_QUERY_KEYS:
            for v in qs.get(key, []):
                if re.search(r"\.(" + _PLAIN_FILE_EXTS + r"|html?|php)$",
                             (v or "").strip(), re.I):
                    return "generic"
        # "?format=jpg" / "?f=mp4": value is a bare extension (anchored).
        for key in _QUERY_FORMAT_KEYS:
            for v in qs.get(key, []):
                if _QUERY_FORMAT_RE.match((v or "").strip()):
                    return "generic"
    except Exception:
        pass
    # No filename signal at all from here on. Page-like addresses keep the
    # yt-dlp default (embedded-player extraction is still worth a try), but
    # any other dotted suffix is a plain file even when we don't know the
    # extension — see _EXT_LIKE_RE above for why.
    if _PAGE_EXT_RE.search(_url_path):
        return "ytdlp"
    # An "@handle" last segment (youtube.com/@some.handle, tiktok.com/@john.doe)
    # is a channel or profile page, not a file, even though handles may hold dots.
    _last_seg = _url_path.rstrip("/").rsplit("/", 1)[-1]
    if _EXT_LIKE_RE.search(_url_path) and not _last_seg.startswith("@"):
        return "generic"
    return "ytdlp"


def _active_bandwidth_profile():
    """Return the first enabled profile whose time window covers now, or None.

    Profiles are dicts: {"name", "start": "HH:MM", "end": "HH:MM",
    "speed_limit_kbps": int}. Overnight windows (start > end) wrap midnight.
    """
    if not STATE.get("bandwidth_profiles_enabled"):
        return None
    now = time.localtime()
    mins = now.tm_hour * 60 + now.tm_min
    for p in STATE.get("bandwidth_profiles") or []:
        try:
            sh, sm = map(int, str(p.get("start", "")).split(":"))
            eh, em = map(int, str(p.get("end", "")).split(":"))
            start = sh * 60 + sm
            end = eh * 60 + em
        except Exception:
            continue
        if start == end:
            continue
        if start < end:
            in_range = start <= mins < end
        else:
            in_range = mins >= start or mins < end
        if in_range:
            return p
    return None


def effective_speed_limit_kbps():
    """Active bandwidth-profile limit if enabled and matching; else global."""
    p = _active_bandwidth_profile()
    if p is not None:
        try:
            return int(p.get("speed_limit_kbps", 0))
        except (TypeError, ValueError):
            return 0
    return int(STATE.get("speed_limit_kbps", 0) or 0)


class SpeedLimiter:
    def __init__(self):
        self.lock = threading.Lock()
        self.last = time.time()
        self.tokens = 0.0

    def consume(self, n):
        limit = effective_speed_limit_kbps() * 1024
        if limit <= 0:
            return
        with self.lock:
            now = time.time()
            elapsed = now - self.last
            self.last = now
            self.tokens = min(limit, self.tokens + elapsed * limit)
            self.tokens -= n
            deficit = -self.tokens
        if deficit > 0:
            time.sleep(deficit / limit)


LIMITER = SpeedLimiter()


def start_bandwidth_profile_watcher():
    """Log when the active bandwidth profile changes (limit applied live)."""
    last = {"key": None}

    def loop():
        while True:
            try:
                p = _active_bandwidth_profile()
                if p is None:
                    key = ("off", effective_speed_limit_kbps())
                else:
                    key = (p.get("name") or p.get("start"),
                           int(p.get("speed_limit_kbps", 0) or 0))
                if key != last["key"]:
                    last["key"] = key
                    if not STATE.get("bandwidth_profiles_enabled"):
                        pass
                    elif p is None:
                        log(f"Bandwidth profile: none active "
                            f"(global {effective_speed_limit_kbps()} KB/s)")
                    else:
                        lim = int(p.get("speed_limit_kbps", 0) or 0)
                        label = p.get("name") or f"{p.get('start')}-{p.get('end')}"
                        lim_s = "unlimited" if lim <= 0 else f"{lim} KB/s"
                        log(f"Bandwidth profile active: {label} → {lim_s}")
            except Exception as e:
                log(f"bandwidth watcher: {e}")
            time.sleep(30)

    threading.Thread(target=loop, daemon=True).start()



def disk_usage_for(path=None):
    """Free/total/used bytes for the drive holding `path` (default:
    STATE['output_dir']). Falls back to HOME if the configured output_dir
    doesn't exist yet (e.g. a per-category override the user hasn't
    created). Returns a dict; never raises."""
    import shutil as _shutil
    target = Path(path) if path else Path(STATE.get("output_dir") or HOME)
    while not target.exists() and target != target.parent:
        target = target.parent
    try:
        total, used, free = _shutil.disk_usage(target)
    except OSError:
        total = used = free = 0
    return {"path": str(target), "total": total, "used": used, "free": free}


def _dest_for(job):
    # NOTE: gui_qt._path_for mirrors this logic - keep the two in sync.
    override = STATE.get("per_category_dirs", {}).get(job["category"])
    base = Path(override) if override else Path(STATE["output_dir"])
    # The category comes from rules, /category and the API, so it is
    # sanitised before it is joined: "..\\x" or "D:\\x" must not escape the
    # output folder. (The per_category_dirs lookup above uses the raw name.)
    cat = "" if override else safe_filename(job["category"] or "Other")
    cat_dir = base / cat if cat else base
    # Session D: per-item playlist jobs land in <category>/<subdir>/. subdir
    # is a real path component (not the legacy playlist_dir display hint).
    sub = safe_filename(job["subdir"]) if job.get("subdir") else ""
    if sub:
        cat_dir = cat_dir / sub
    # The name is shortened when the whole path would pass the Windows limit.
    return cat_dir / truncate_for_dir(base, cat, sub, safe_filename(job["filename"]))


def stat_for(job):
    dest = _dest_for(job)
    dest.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    # _dest_for shortened an over-long name: keep job["filename"] in sync
    # (the GUI builds its own path from it).
    if dest.name != safe_filename(job["filename"]):
        job["filename"] = dest.name
    # Collision handling: "name (2).ext" — but ONLY when the job hasn't
    # started yet (no .part file, no bytes downloaded), otherwise we'd
    # rename a file mid-resume. Side effect on job["filename"] is
    # intentional: _dest_for stays pure and every caller agrees on the name.
    part = dest.with_suffix(dest.suffix + ".part")
    segments = []
    if dest.parent.exists():
        segments = list(dest.parent.glob(glob.escape(dest.name) + ".part*"))
    if (not part.exists() and not segments
            and not job.get("size_done") and dest.exists()):
        unique = _unique_path(dest)
        if unique.name != dest.name:
            job["filename"] = unique.name
            dest = unique
    return dest





# ------------------------------------------------------------------ v5 ----
# Proxy, naming, source-site and archive helpers.

_PROXY_SCHEMES = ("http", "https", "socks4", "socks5", "socks5h")


def _is_yt_host(host):
    host = (host or "").lower()
    return host == "youtu.be" or host == "youtube.com" or host.endswith(".youtube.com")


def proxy_for(url):
    """Proxy URL to use for `url`, or None. Honors proxy_scope."""
    p = str(STATE.get("proxy_url") or "").strip()
    if not p:
        return None
    try:
        u = urlparse(p)
    except ValueError:
        return None
    if u.scheme.lower() not in _PROXY_SCHEMES or not u.netloc:
        return None
    if STATE.get("proxy_scope", "youtube") == "all":
        return p
    try:
        host = urlparse(url or "").hostname
    except ValueError:
        return None
    return p if _is_yt_host(host) else None


def proxies_for(url):
    """requests-style proxies dict, or None. SOCKS needs PySocks; without
    it the proxy is skipped (and logged once) rather than failing every
    request."""
    p = proxy_for(url)
    if not p:
        return None
    if p.lower().startswith("socks"):
        try:
            import socks  # noqa: F401  (PySocks)
        except ImportError:
            if not getattr(proxies_for, "_warned", False):
                proxies_for._warned = True
                log("proxy: SOCKS proxy set but PySocks isn't installed; "
                    "generic downloads will go direct (yt-dlp is unaffected)")
            return None
    return {"http": p, "https": p}


_JUNK_STEMS = {
    "watch", "index", "download", "downloads", "video", "videos", "playlist",
    "file", "stream", "master", "manifest", "embed", "player", "view", "get",
    "status", "document", "media", "content", "default", "untitled", "null",
    "undefined", "unknown", "live", "clip",
}
_JUNK_PATTERN_RE = re.compile(
    r"(?:video|download|file|watch|playlist|media)[ _-]?\(?\d*\)?(?: \(\d+\))*")
# Raw URL basenames that name a stream rather than a title: HLS/DASH variant
# playlists (index-f2-v1-a1, chunklist_720p, media_0, seg-12-v1-a1), bare
# quality labels (720p, 1080), hash-like ids and master/manifest leftovers.
_JUNK_URL_RE = re.compile(
    r"(?:index|playlist|master|manifest|main|stream|video|audio|chunklist|media|"
    r"variant|rendition|segment|seg|frag|fragment|init|hls|dash)"
    r"(?:[ _.-]?(?:f\d+|v\d+|a\d+|s\d+|\d{1,5}p?|\d{3,4}p|[0-9a-f]{6,}))*"
    r"|(?:f\d+|v\d+|a\d+)(?:-(?:f\d+|v\d+|a\d+))+"
    r"|\d{3,4}p?"
    r"|[0-9a-f]{16,}",             # long hex ids
    re.I)
_TITLE_SUFFIX_RE = re.compile(
    r"\s*[-|\u2013\u2014:]\s*(?:YouTube|Twitch|Twitter|Vimeo|Facebook|Instagram|"
    r"TikTok|Reddit|Dailymotion|Bilibili)\s*$", re.I)
_TITLE_X_RE = re.compile(r"\s*/\s*X\s*$")


def is_junk_stem(stem):
    """True for names that say nothing: 'watch', 'index', pure numbers,
    'watch (2) (2)', 'video_1', etc."""
    s = (stem or "").strip().lower()
    if len(s) < 2:
        return True
    if s in _JUNK_STEMS or s.isdigit():
        return True
    if _JUNK_PATTERN_RE.fullmatch(s) or _JUNK_URL_RE.fullmatch(s):
        return True
    # Hyphen/underscore-joined tokens that are ALL stream tokens, e.g.
    # "index-f2-v1-a1" or "master_720p".
    toks = [t for t in re.split(r"[-_. ]+", s) if t]
    return bool(toks) and all(_JUNK_URL_RE.fullmatch(t) for t in toks)


def clean_title(title):
    """Drop notification counts like '(3) ' and ' - YouTube'-style suffixes."""
    t = re.sub(r"^\s*\(\d+\+?\)\s*", "", title or "")
    t = _TITLE_SUFFIX_RE.sub("", t)
    t = _TITLE_X_RE.sub("", t)
    return t.strip()


def site_host(url):
    try:
        h = (urlparse(url or "").hostname or "").lower()
    except ValueError:
        h = ""
    return h[4:] if h.startswith("www.") else h


def source_site_for(*urls):
    """First usable site domain among the given URLs (page, referer, file)."""
    for u in urls:
        h = site_host(u)
        if h and h not in ("localhost",) and not re.fullmatch(r"[\d.:]+", h):
            return h
    return None


_TYPE_LABELS = {"video": "video", "audio": "audio", "music": "audio",
                "image": "image", "images": "image", "document": "doc",
                "documents": "doc", "archive": "archive", "archives": "archive",
                "program": "app", "programs": "app", "other": "file",
                "generic": "file"}


def generated_name(url, ftype=None, ext=None):
    """Fallback stem when nothing better exists: {domain}_{date}_{type}.
    Pass ext (with or without the dot) to get the full "{domain}_{date}_{type}.{ext}"
    filename; without it the bare stem is returned, as before. ftype is a
    category/type name ("Video", "video", ...); when omitted the type is
    guessed from the URL's extension."""
    host = site_host(url)
    parts = host.split(".")
    label = parts[-2] if len(parts) >= 2 else (parts[0] if parts and parts[0] else "download")
    label = re.sub(r"[^A-Za-z0-9]+", "", label) or "download"
    if not ext:
        m = re.search(r"\.([A-Za-z0-9]{2,5})(?:[?#]|$)", urlparse(url or "").path or "")
        guess = m.group(1).lower() if m else ""
    else:
        guess = ext.lstrip(".").lower()
    kind = _TYPE_LABELS.get((ftype or "").strip().lower(), "")
    if not kind:
        if guess in ("m3u8", "mpd", "mp4", "m4v", "mov", "webm", "mkv", "avi", "ts", "flv"):
            kind = "video"
        elif guess in ("mp3", "m4a", "aac", "wav", "flac", "opus", "ogg"):
            kind = "audio"
        elif guess in ("jpg", "jpeg", "png", "gif", "webp", "avif", "bmp"):
            kind = "image"
        else:
            kind = "file"
    stem = safe_filename(f"{label}_{time.strftime('%Y-%m-%d')}_{kind}")
    if ext:
        # HLS/DASH manifests are downloaded as mp4, never as .m3u8/.mpd.
        e = "mp4" if guess in ("m3u8", "mpd") else guess
        return f"{stem}.{e}" if e else stem
    return stem


_ARCHIVE_LOCK = threading.Lock()


def archive_path():
    return HOME / "archive.txt"


def archive_ids():
    """Set of 'extractor id' lines recorded as downloaded (yt-dlp format)."""
    try:
        with _ARCHIVE_LOCK:
            return {ln.strip() for ln in
                    archive_path().read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines()
                    if ln.strip()}
    except OSError:
        return set()


def archive_add(extractor, vid):
    """Record a finished download so playlist pickers can flag it later."""
    if not extractor or not vid:
        return
    line = f"{str(extractor).lower()} {vid}"
    try:
        with _ARCHIVE_LOCK:
            p = archive_path()
            p.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
            try:
                if line in {ln.strip() for ln in p.read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines()}:
                    return
            except OSError:
                pass
            with open(p, "a", encoding="utf-8") as f:
                f.write(line + "\n")
    except OSError as e:
        log(f"archive write failed: {e}")


def icons_dir():
    return HOME / "icons""""sounds.py: completion sound for Video Grabber (v5.5).

The old behavior was winsound.MessageBeep, which plays a Windows *system*
sound and is silent when the Windows sound scheme is "No Sounds". This module
plays real audio files instead:

  1. a bundled preset (sounds\\<id>.wav next to the app code; if the file is
     missing it is synthesized into <data folder>\\sounds\\ on first use, so a
     preset always exists), or the user's own .wav / .mp3 file;
  2. if that fails or the file is missing: winsound.MessageBeep;
  3. if that fails too: silent.

Every step is logged, so a silent failure shows up in the log.
"""
import ctypes
import itertools
import math
import struct
import sys
import threading
import wave
from pathlib import Path

try:
    from logging_setup import log
except Exception:                      # standalone use (tests)
    def log(msg):
        print(msg)

try:
    import settings as _settings
    STATE = _settings.STATE
except Exception:                      # standalone use (tests)
    _settings, STATE = None, {}


def _home():
    # Read at call time: settings.set_paths() can move HOME (portable mode).
    return Path(_settings.HOME) if _settings is not None else Path(".")

DEFAULT_PRESET = "chime"
CUSTOM = "custom"
# id -> label shown in Settings
PRESETS = {
    "chime": "Chime",
    "ding": "Ding",
    "pop": "Pop",
    "double": "Double beep",
}
_RATE = 44100
_ALIAS = itertools.count(1)


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- synthesis
def _tone(buf, freq, start, dur, amp, decay, harmonics=((1, 1.0),)):
    """Add a decaying sine (plus optional overtones) into the sample buffer."""
    n0 = int(start * _RATE)
    n = int(dur * _RATE)
    for i in range(n):
        idx = n0 + i
        if idx >= len(buf):
            break
        t = i / _RATE
        env = math.exp(-t * decay) * min(1.0, i / (0.004 * _RATE))   # 4 ms attack: no click
        s = sum(a * math.sin(2 * math.pi * freq * h * t) for h, a in harmonics)
        buf[idx] += amp * env * s


def _synth(preset):
    """Return 16-bit mono samples (list of ints) for a preset id."""
    if preset == "ding":
        buf = [0.0] * int(0.9 * _RATE)
        _tone(buf, 880.0, 0.0, 0.9, 0.55, 5.5, ((1, 1.0), (2, 0.25), (3, 0.08)))
    elif preset == "pop":
        buf = [0.0] * int(0.25 * _RATE)
        _tone(buf, 520.0, 0.0, 0.2, 0.6, 22.0, ((1, 1.0), (2, 0.2)))
    elif preset == "double":
        buf = [0.0] * int(0.5 * _RATE)
        _tone(buf, 880.0, 0.0, 0.14, 0.5, 14.0)
        _tone(buf, 880.0, 0.2, 0.14, 0.5, 14.0)
    else:                                  # "chime": three rising notes
        buf = [0.0] * int(1.3 * _RATE)
        for k, f in enumerate((1046.5, 1318.5, 1568.0)):
            _tone(buf, f, 0.0 + 0.1 * k, 1.0, 0.32, 4.5, ((1, 1.0), (2, 0.2)))
    peak = max(1e-9, max(abs(x) for x in buf))
    scale = min(1.0, 0.85 / peak)
    return [int(max(-1.0, min(1.0, x * scale)) * 32767) for x in buf]


def write_preset(preset, path):
    """Write a preset to a 16-bit mono 44.1 kHz .wav file."""
    samples = _synth(preset)
    path = Path(path)
    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    with wave.open(str(path), "wb") as w:
        w.setnchannels(1)
        w.setsampwidth(2)
        w.setframerate(_RATE)
        w.writeframes(struct.pack("<%dh" % len(samples), *samples))
    return path


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- resolving
def bundled_dir():
    return Path(__file__).resolve().parent / "sounds"


def preset_path(preset):
    """Path to a preset's .wav: the bundled file if it shipped, else one
    synthesized into <data folder>\\sounds\\ (created once)."""
    if preset not in PRESETS:
        preset = DEFAULT_PRESET
    p = bundled_dir() / f"{preset}.wav"
    if p.is_file():
        return p
    user = _home() / "sounds" / f"{preset}.wav"
    if not user.is_file():
        log(f"sound: bundled {preset}.wav not found, generating {user}")
        write_preset(preset, user)
    return user


def resolve(preset=None, custom_path=None):
    """(path, description). path is None when nothing usable is selected."""
    preset = preset if preset is not None else STATE.get("completion_sound", DEFAULT_PRESET)
    custom_path = custom_path if custom_path is not None else STATE.get("completion_sound_path", "")
    if preset == CUSTOM:
        p = Path(str(custom_path or ""))
        if str(custom_path or "").strip() and p.is_file():
            return p, f"custom file {p}"
        return None, f"custom file missing ({custom_path or 'no file chosen'})"
    return preset_path(preset), f"preset {preset}"


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- playback
def _mci(cmd):
    """One MCI command (winmm). Raises RuntimeError with Windows' own text."""
    winmm = ctypes.windll.winmm
    buf = ctypes.create_unicode_buffer(256)
    rc = winmm.mciSendStringW(cmd, buf, 255, None)
    if rc:
        err = ctypes.create_unicode_buffer(256)
        winmm.mciGetErrorStringW(rc, err, 255)
        raise RuntimeError(f"MCI error {rc}: {err.value} ({cmd})")
    return buf.value


def _play_mci(path):
    """mp3 (and any non-wav) through MCI. Opens synchronously so a bad file
    raises here; the playback itself runs in a daemon thread."""
    alias = f"vgsnd{next(_ALIAS)}"
    kind = " type mpegvideo" if path.suffix.lower() == ".mp3" else ""
    _mci(f'open "{path}"{kind} alias {alias}')

    def run():
        try:
            _mci(f"play {alias} wait")
        except Exception as e:
            log(f"sound: MCI playback failed: {e}")
        finally:
            try:
                _mci(f"close {alias}")
            except Exception:
                pass

    threading.Thread(target=run, daemon=True, name="vg-sound").start()


def _play_file(path):
    if sys.platform != "win32":
        raise RuntimeError("sound playback is Windows-only")
    if path.suffix.lower() == ".wav":
        import winsound
        # SND_FILENAME plays the file itself, so the Windows sound scheme
        # ("No Sounds") doesn't matter. SND_NODEFAULT: no fallback beep.
        winsound.PlaySound(str(path), winsound.SND_FILENAME | winsound.SND_ASYNC
                           | winsound.SND_NODEFAULT)
    else:
        _play_mci(path)


def _beep():
    import winsound
    winsound.MessageBeep(winsound.MB_ICONASTERISK)


def play_completion_sound(preset=None, custom_path=None, why="completion"):
    """Play the selected sound. Selection defaults to STATE; Settings'
    Test button passes the unsaved choice. Returns True when the file was
    started, False when it fell back to MessageBeep or stayed silent."""
    path, desc = None, ""
    try:
        path, desc = resolve(preset, custom_path)
        if path is not None:
            log(f"sound ({why}): playing {desc} -> {path}")
            _play_file(path)
            return True
        log(f"sound ({why}): {desc}; falling back to MessageBeep")
    except Exception as e:
        log(f"sound ({why}): couldn't play {desc or 'selected sound'}: {e}; "
            "falling back to MessageBeep")
    try:
        _beep()
        log(f"sound ({why}): MessageBeep played (silent if the Windows sound "
            "scheme is set to No Sounds)")
    except Exception as e:
        log(f"sound ({why}): MessageBeep failed too ({e}); staying silent")
    return False
"""
sound_generator.py -- Procedural sound effects generator for Video Grabber.

Stop hunting for notification sounds online: this tool synthesises short
.wav files from scratch, lets you preview them instantly, and saves the
ones you like into ./sounds/ for sounds.py to play on download completion.

Only the standard library is used for synthesis / file handling
(wave, struct, math, random, pathlib, os -- plus winsound for playback,
which is also standard library on Windows) together with PySide6 for the UI.

Run it with:
    python sound_generator.py

Settings > Sounds opens SoundOptionsDialog (open_sound_options below): three
sounds from three different style families out of a library of 100 style
profiles, a length choice (1 / 3 / 5 / 10 s), Play, a name box, Save to
Library and Save as Default. Both save buttons write <home>/sounds/<name>.wav;
Save as Default also makes it the completion sound. That engine needs numpy;
the older SoundGeneratorWindow below does not.
"""

import importlib
import math
import os
import random
import re
import struct
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile
import wave
from pathlib import Path

# winsound is Windows-only (and required for SND_ASYNC playback).
# Guard the import so this file still *runs* on macOS/Linux for testing,
# where playback falls back to PySide6's QSoundEffect instead.
try:
    import winsound
except ImportError:  # Not on Windows
    winsound = None

from PySide6.QtCore import Qt, QThread, QTimer, QUrl, Signal
from PySide6.QtGui import QAction, QColor, QPainter, QPen
from PySide6.QtWidgets import (
    QApplication,
    QComboBox,

    QListWidget,
    QMainWindow,
    QMessageBox,
    QPushButton,
    QVBoxLayout,
    QWidget,
)

# but keep the import defensive in case QtMultimedia isn't installed.
try:
    from PySide6.QtMultimedia import QSoundEffect
except ImportError:  # pragma: no cover
    QSoundEffect = None


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Constants
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

SAMPLE_RATE = 44100          # Hz -- CD quality, matches sounds.py playback
CHANNELS = 1                 # Mono
SAMPLE_WIDTH = 2             # Bytes per sample -> 16-bit audio
ATTACK_SECONDS = 0.004       # 4 ms attack, prevents clicks at note starts
TARGET_PEAK = 0.9            # Normalise to 90% of full scale (headroom)

BASE_DIR = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
SOUNDS_DIR = BASE_DIR / "sounds"            # ./sounds/ next to this script
# Scratch file for previews lives in the OS temp folder, NOT in the app
# folder -- otherwise an unsaved preview is left behind as junk when the
# app closes. The OS cleans its temp folder up by itself.
# Note: TEMP is the Windows variable; on systems without it we fall back
# to BASE_DIR so the tool still works.
TEMP_PATH = Path(os.environ.get("TEMP", BASE_DIR)) / "temp_preview.wav"


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Synthesis helpers
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def _wave_sample(waveform: str, phase: float) -> float:
    """One oscillator sample for `waveform` at `phase` radians (Batch 4)."""
    if waveform == "square":
        return 1.0 if math.sin(phase) > 0 else -1.0
    if waveform == "sawtooth":
        return 2.0 * ((phase / (2 * math.pi)) % 1.0) - 1.0
    if waveform == "triangle":
        return 2.0 * abs(2.0 * ((phase / (2 * math.pi)) % 1.0) - 1.0) - 1.0
    if waveform == "noise":
        return random.uniform(-1.0, 1.0)
    return math.sin(phase)  # "sine" (and any unknown name) stays a sine


def _add_tone(
    buffer: list[float],
    start_seconds: float,
    duration_seconds: float,
    frequency: float,
    amplitude: float = 1.0,
    decay: float = 6.0,
    overtones: tuple[tuple[float, float], ...] = ((1.0, 1.0),),
    sweep_to: float | None = None,
    waveform: str = "sine",
) -> None:
    """Mix one tone into ``buffer`` (a list of float samples).

    Args:
        buffer:    Float sample buffer, modified in place.
        start_seconds: When the tone starts.
        duration_seconds: How long it lasts.
        frequency: Starting frequency in Hz.
        amplitude: Peak amplitude of this tone (before normalisation).
        decay:     Exponential decay rate -- higher = fades faster.
                   Use ~0 for a beep that stays level until it ends.
        overtones: (frequency_multiplier, relative_amplitude) pairs.
                   (1.0, 1.0) is a pure sine; extra pairs add harmonics.
        sweep_to:  If given, glide the frequency to this value over the
                   tone's duration (used by the laser / thump sweeps).
        waveform:  Oscillator shape for this tone (Batch 4): "sine",
                   "square", "sawtooth", "triangle" or "noise".
    """
    start = int(start_seconds * SAMPLE_RATE)
    length = int(duration_seconds * SAMPLE_RATE)
    attack = max(1, int(ATTACK_SECONDS * SAMPLE_RATE))
    release = min(length // 2, int(0.008 * SAMPLE_RATE))  # 8 ms fade-out

    phase = 0.0
    for i in range(length):
        index = start + i
        if index >= len(buffer):
            break

        t = i / SAMPLE_RATE
        progress = i / max(1, length - 1)

        # Frequency for this sample (constant, or sweeping for a blip).
        if sweep_to is None:
            freq = frequency
        else:
            freq = frequency + (sweep_to - frequency) * progress
        phase += 2.0 * math.pi * freq / SAMPLE_RATE

        # Envelope: 4 ms linear attack -> exponential decay -> short release.
        if i < attack:
            envelope = i / attack
        else:
            envelope = math.exp(-decay * max(0.0, t - ATTACK_SECONDS))
        if release and i >= length - release:
            envelope *= (length - i) / release

        # Sum the fundamental and any overtones.
        sample = 0.0
        for multiplier, relative_amp in overtones:
            sample += relative_amp * _wave_sample(waveform, phase * multiplier)

        buffer[index] += amplitude * envelope * sample


PROFILES = ("Random", "Retro 8-Bit", "16-Bit Console", "Modern UI",
            "Sci-Fi / Laser", "Chime / Marimba", "Noise / Impact")
_CONCRETE_PROFILES = PROFILES[1:]


def _render_style(profile: str) -> tuple[list[float], int]:
    """Render one Batch 4 profile into a float sample buffer.

    Returns (buffer, num_layers) -- num_layers is the number of
    _add_tone layers mixed into the buffer, which the UI reports next
    to the profile name.
    """
    if profile == "Retro 8-Bit":
        # 3 square-wave notes stepping up: root, major third (+4
        # semitones), fifth (+7) -- the classic 8-bit arpeggio.
        buffer = [0.0] * int(0.55 * SAMPLE_RATE)
        base = random.choice([523.25, 587.33, 659.25])  # C5 / D5 / E5
        for step, semitones in enumerate((0, 4, 7)):
            freq = base * (2.0 ** (semitones / 12.0))
            _add_tone(buffer, start_seconds=step * 0.09, duration_seconds=0.22,
                      frequency=freq, amplitude=0.7, decay=8.0,
                      waveform="square")
        return buffer, 3

    if profile == "16-Bit Console":
        # Sawtooth lead, a triangle harmony a fifth up (+7 semitones),
        # and a soft triangle root an octave down -- a 16-bit chord stab.
        buffer = [0.0] * int(0.80 * SAMPLE_RATE)
        base = random.choice([392.00, 440.00, 523.25])  # G4 / A4 / C5
        _add_tone(buffer, start_seconds=0.0, duration_seconds=0.50,
                  frequency=base, amplitude=0.65, decay=5.0,
                  waveform="sawtooth")
        _add_tone(buffer, start_seconds=0.0, duration_seconds=0.50,
                  frequency=base * (2.0 ** (7 / 12.0)), amplitude=0.5,
                  decay=5.0, waveform="triangle")
        _add_tone(buffer, start_seconds=0.02, duration_seconds=0.60,
                  frequency=base / 2.0, amplitude=0.55, decay=4.0,
                  waveform="triangle")
        return buffer, 3

    if profile == "Modern UI":
        # 1-2 short triangle blips, the second (when present) a fourth
        # up (+5 semitones) -- clean, soft UI confirmation chirps.
        buffer = [0.0] * int(0.40 * SAMPLE_RATE)
        base = random.choice([880.00, 1046.50])  # A5 / C6
        layers = random.choice([1, 2])
        _add_tone(buffer, start_seconds=0.0, duration_seconds=0.12,
                  frequency=base, amplitude=0.8, decay=11.0,
                  waveform="triangle")
        if layers == 2:
            _add_tone(buffer, start_seconds=0.08, duration_seconds=0.16,
                      frequency=base * (2.0 ** (5 / 12.0)), amplitude=0.8,
                      decay=10.0, waveform="triangle")
        return buffer, layers

    if profile == "Sci-Fi / Laser":
        # Sawtooth pitch sweep diving down, with a short noise burst
        # layered over it for the zap's edge.
        buffer = [0.0] * int(0.60 * SAMPLE_RATE)
        _add_tone(buffer, start_seconds=0.0, duration_seconds=0.45,
                  frequency=random.uniform(1200.0, 1600.0), sweep_to=110.0,
                  amplitude=0.75, decay=3.5, waveform="sawtooth")
        _add_tone(buffer, start_seconds=0.05, duration_seconds=0.18,
                  frequency=2000.0, amplitude=0.35, decay=16.0,
                  waveform="noise")
        return buffer, 2

    if profile == "Chime / Marimba":
        # Sine base plus two higher sine overtone layers, each decaying
        # faster than the one below it -- a struck-bar chime.
        buffer = [0.0] * int(1.20 * SAMPLE_RATE)
        base = random.choice([659.25, 783.99, 880.00, 1046.50])
        _add_tone(buffer, start_seconds=0.0, duration_seconds=1.20,
                  frequency=base, amplitude=1.0, decay=4.0, waveform="sine")
        _add_tone(buffer, start_seconds=0.0, duration_seconds=0.80,
                  frequency=base * 2.0, amplitude=0.40, decay=6.5,
                  waveform="sine")
        _add_tone(buffer, start_seconds=0.0, duration_seconds=0.50,
                  frequency=base * 2.76, amplitude=0.18, decay=9.0,
                  waveform="sine")
        return buffer, 3

    if profile == "Noise / Impact":
        # Deep sine thump gliding down, plus a white-noise burst --
        # a soft impact / thud.
        buffer = [0.0] * int(0.50 * SAMPLE_RATE)
        _add_tone(buffer, start_seconds=0.0, duration_seconds=0.35,
                  frequency=110.0, sweep_to=48.0, amplitude=1.0, decay=5.0,
                  waveform="sine")
        _add_tone(buffer, start_seconds=0.0, duration_seconds=0.22,
                  frequency=1500.0, amplitude=0.45, decay=14.0,
                  waveform="noise")
        return buffer, 2

    raise ValueError(f"Unknown profile: {profile}")


def _normalise(buffer: list[float]) -> None:
    """Scale ``buffer`` in place so its peak sits at TARGET_PEAK."""
    peak = max((abs(s) for s in buffer), default=0.0)
    if peak > 0:
        scale = TARGET_PEAK / peak
        for i, sample in enumerate(buffer):
            buffer[i] = sample * scale


def _write_wav(path: Path, buffer: list[float]) -> None:
    """Write float samples (-1.0..1.0) as a 16-bit mono .wav file."""
    frames = b"".join(
        struct.pack("<h", int(max(-1.0, min(1.0, s)) * 32767))
        for s in buffer
    )
    with wave.open(str(path), "wb") as wav:
        wav.setnchannels(CHANNELS)
        wav.setsampwidth(SAMPLE_WIDTH)
        wav.setframerate(SAMPLE_RATE)
        wav.writeframes(frames)


def generate_sound(
    output_path: str | Path, profile: str = "Random",
) -> tuple[Path, str, int]:
    """Synthesise a notification sound for `profile` and write a .wav.

    `profile` is one of PROFILES (see the generator window's combo);
    "Random" (or an unknown name) picks a concrete profile at random.
    A 4 ms attack is applied to every note and the result is normalised.

    Args:
        output_path: Where to write the .wav file.
        profile:     Which Batch 4 profile to render.

    Returns:
        (path, profile_name, num_layers) -- so the UI can tell you what
        it generated and how many layers were mixed into it.
    """
    output_path = Path(output_path)
    if output_path.parent != Path(""):
        output_path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

    if profile not in _CONCRETE_PROFILES:
        profile = random.choice(_CONCRETE_PROFILES)
    buffer, num_layers = _render_style(profile)
    _normalise(buffer)
    _write_wav(output_path, buffer)
    return output_path, profile, num_layers


def read_wav_samples(path: str | Path) -> list[float]:
    """Read a 16-bit .wav back into float mono samples (for the waveform).

    Our own files are mono, but a file dropped into ./sounds/ by hand may
    be stereo -- in that case the channels are averaged per frame rather
    than interleaved (which would draw a garbled waveform). Files that
    aren't 16-bit return an empty list instead of mis-decoding.
    """
    with wave.open(str(path), "rb") as wav:
        if wav.getsampwidth() != SAMPLE_WIDTH:
            return []
        channels = max(1, wav.getnchannels())
        raw = wav.readframes(wav.getnframes())
    count = len(raw) // SAMPLE_WIDTH
    ints = struct.unpack(f"<{count}h", raw[: count * SAMPLE_WIDTH])
    if channels == 1:
        return [s / 32768.0 for s in ints]
    # De-interleave: average each frame's channels into one mono sample.
    return [
        sum(ints[i:i + channels]) / channels / 32768.0
        for i in range(0, count - channels + 1, channels)
    ]


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Playback
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def stop_playback(fallback_player=None) -> None:
    """Stop any async preview that is currently playing.

    This matters before overwriting, moving or deleting a .wav: on
    Windows a file that winsound is playing can be locked, and a new
    PlaySound on top of an old one is exactly the confusion the
    Generate-button debounce is trying to avoid.
    """
    if winsound is not None:
        try:
            winsound.PlaySound(None, winsound.SND_PURGE)
        except RuntimeError:
            pass
    elif fallback_player is not None:
        fallback_player.stop()


def play_wav_async(path: str | Path, fallback_player=None) -> None:
    """Play a .wav without blocking the UI.

    On Windows this uses winsound with SND_ASYNC, exactly as sounds.py
    expects. Elsewhere it falls back to a QSoundEffect if one is supplied.
    A corrupt / unreadable file must never crash the UI, so playback
    errors are swallowed here -- generation and saving still work.
    """
    path = Path(path)
    if winsound is not None:
        try:
            winsound.PlaySound(
                str(path),
                winsound.SND_FILENAME | winsound.SND_ASYNC,
            )
        except RuntimeError:
            pass
    elif fallback_player is not None:
        fallback_player.setSource(QUrl.fromLocalFile(str(path)))
        fallback_player.play()
    # If neither is available there's simply no preview -- generation
    # and saving still work, so don't crash the tool over audio output.


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Waveform widget
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

class WaveformWidget(QWidget):
    """Simple QWidget that draws the amplitude waveform with QPainter."""

    def __init__(self, parent=None) -> None:
        super().__init__(parent)
        self._samples: list[float] = []
        self.setMinimumHeight(130)
        self.setMinimumWidth(280)

    def set_samples(self, samples: list[float]) -> None:
        """Replace the displayed waveform and repaint."""
        self._samples = samples
        self.update()

    def load_wav(self, path: str | Path) -> None:
        """Load a .wav file and display its waveform."""
        try:
            self.set_samples(read_wav_samples(path))
        except (OSError, EOFError, wave.Error):
            # Truncated / non-wav file in the folder: show "no waveform"
            # rather than taking the whole window down with it.
            self.set_samples([])

    def paintEvent(self, event) -> None:  # noqa: N802 - Qt naming
        painter = QPainter(self)
        painter.setRenderHint(QPainter.RenderHint.Antialiasing)

        # Background + centre (zero) line.
        painter.fillRect(self.rect(), QColor(30, 30, 36))
        mid_y = self.height() / 2
        painter.setPen(QPen(QColor(90, 90, 100), 1))
        painter.drawLine(0, int(mid_y), self.width(), int(mid_y))

        if not self._samples:
            painter.setPen(QColor(150, 150, 160))
            painter.drawText(self.rect(), Qt.AlignmentFlag.AlignCenter,
                             "Generate a sound to see its waveform")
            return

        # Min/max per horizontal pixel: accurate even for long files,
        # and cheap -- one vertical line per pixel of width. Buckets are
        # mapped proportionally across the whole file, so the tail of
        # the sound isn't cut off when len(samples) % width != 0.
        painter.setPen(QPen(QColor(80, 220, 160), 1))
        width = max(1, self.width())
        total = len(self._samples)
        half_height = (self.height() / 2) - 6

        for x in range(width):
            start = x * total // width
            end = max(start + 1, (x + 1) * total // width)
            chunk = self._samples[start:end]
            if not chunk:
                break
            y_top = mid_y - (max(chunk) * half_height)
            y_bottom = mid_y - (min(chunk) * half_height)
            # Ensure a silent chunk still shows as a 1px dot on the line.
            painter.drawLine(x, int(y_top), x, int(max(y_bottom, y_top + 1)))


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Main window
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

class SoundGeneratorWindow(QMainWindow):
    """Preview, name, save and manage procedurally generated sounds.

    This works two ways:
      * Standalone: run this file and it is the whole app (see main()).
      * Embedded in Video Grabber: pass the app's main window as
        ``parent`` and it opens as a child window of the app -- see
        open_sound_generator() below, which is what a menu item /
        toolbar button in Video Grabber should call.

    Args:
        parent:     Optional parent widget (Video Grabber's main window).
        sounds_dir: Folder to save to / list from. Defaults to ./sounds/
                    next to this file. Pass Video Grabber's real sounds
                    folder here if sounds.py keeps sounds somewhere else.
    """

    def __init__(self, parent=None, sounds_dir: str | Path | None = None) -> None:
        super().__init__(parent)
        self.setWindowTitle("Video Grabber -- Sound Generator")
        self.resize(760, 360)

        self.sounds_dir = Path(sounds_dir) if sounds_dir else SOUNDS_DIR
        self.temp_path: Path | None = None

        # Fallback player (only actually used when winsound is missing).
        self._fallback_player = QSoundEffect(self) if QSoundEffect else None

        self.sounds_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

        # --- Left side: generation + preview + saving -------------------
        # Batch 4: profile picker above Generate.
        self.profile_combo = QComboBox()
        self.profile_combo.addItems(PROFILES)
        self.profile_combo.setToolTip(
            "Sound profile for the next generated sound")

        self.generate_button = QPushButton("Generate New Sound")
        self.generate_button.setMinimumHeight(56)
        self.generate_button.setStyleSheet("font-size: 18px; font-weight: bold;")
        self.generate_button.clicked.connect(self.on_generate)

        self.waveform = WaveformWidget()

        self.style_label = QLabel("No sound generated yet.")
        self.style_label.setAlignment(Qt.AlignmentFlag.AlignCenter)

        name_row = QHBoxLayout()
        name_row.addWidget(QLabel("Sound Name:"))
        self.name_input = QLineEdit(f"custom_{random.randint(1000, 9999)}")
        name_row.addWidget(self.name_input)

        self.save_button = QPushButton("Save to Sounds Folder")
        self.save_button.setEnabled(False)  # Nothing to save until generated
        self.save_button.clicked.connect(self.on_save)

        left_layout = QVBoxLayout()
        left_layout.addWidget(self.profile_combo)
        left_layout.addWidget(self.generate_button)
        left_layout.addWidget(self.waveform)
        # Batch 4: preview transport for the unsaved sound, below the
        # waveform. Disabled until a sound has been generated.
        preview_row = QHBoxLayout()
        self.preview_play_btn = QPushButton("▶ Play Preview")
        self.preview_play_btn.setEnabled(False)
        self.preview_play_btn.clicked.connect(self._preview_play)
        self.preview_stop_btn = QPushButton("⏹ Stop")
        self.preview_stop_btn.setEnabled(False)
        self.preview_stop_btn.clicked.connect(self._preview_stop)
        preview_row.addWidget(self.preview_play_btn)
        preview_row.addWidget(self.preview_stop_btn)
        left_layout.addLayout(preview_row)
        left_layout.addWidget(self.style_label)
        left_layout.addLayout(name_row)
        left_layout.addWidget(self.save_button)
        left_layout.addStretch()

        # --- Right side: existing sounds in ./sounds/ ---------------------
        self.sounds_list = QListWidget()
        self.sounds_list.itemDoubleClicked.connect(lambda _item: self.on_play())
        self.sounds_list.currentRowChanged.connect(self._on_selection_changed)

        # Kept as attributes so they can be disabled when nothing is
        # selected -- otherwise clicking them silently does nothing,
        # which looks like the app has hung.
        self.play_button = QPushButton("Play")
        self.play_button.clicked.connect(self.on_play)
        self.play_button.setEnabled(False)
        self.delete_button = QPushButton("Delete")
        self.delete_button.clicked.connect(self.on_delete)
        self.delete_button.setEnabled(False)

        list_buttons = QHBoxLayout()
        list_buttons.addWidget(self.play_button)
        list_buttons.addWidget(self.delete_button)

        right_layout = QVBoxLayout()
        right_layout.addWidget(QLabel("Saved sounds (./sounds/)"))
        right_layout.addWidget(self.sounds_list)
        right_layout.addLayout(list_buttons)

        # --- Assemble ------------------------------------------------------
        central = QWidget()
        main_layout = QHBoxLayout(central)
        main_layout.addLayout(left_layout, stretch=3)
        main_layout.addLayout(right_layout, stretch=2)
        self.setCentralWidget(central)

        self.refresh_list()

    # -- Generation ---------------------------------------------------------

    def on_generate(self) -> None:
        """Generate a temp sound, play it immediately, show its waveform."""
        # Debounce: disable the button for 0.5s so a double-click can't
        # fire two generations / two async plays at the same instant --
        # winsound handles that badly (often playing neither sound).
        self.generate_button.setEnabled(False)
        QTimer.singleShot(500, self._re_enable_generate)

        # Stop the previous preview before overwriting the temp file it
        # may still be playing from (a playing file can be locked).
        stop_playback(self._fallback_player)

        try:
            self.temp_path, profile, num_layers = generate_sound(
                TEMP_PATH, self.profile_combo.currentText())
        except OSError as exc:
            QMessageBox.warning(self, "Generation failed",
                                f"Could not write the preview file:\n{exc}")
            return

        self.waveform.load_wav(self.temp_path)
        self.style_label.setText(
            f"Profile: {profile} (Layers: {num_layers}) -- press Save to keep it")
        self.save_button.setEnabled(True)
        self.preview_play_btn.setEnabled(True)
        self.preview_stop_btn.setEnabled(True)
        play_wav_async(self.temp_path, self._fallback_player)

    def _re_enable_generate(self) -> None:
        try:
            self.generate_button.setEnabled(True)
        except RuntimeError:
            pass  # window closed before the debounce fired

    def _preview_play(self) -> None:
        """Replay the current unsaved preview (Batch 4)."""
        if self.temp_path is not None:
            play_wav_async(self.temp_path, self._fallback_player)

    def _preview_stop(self) -> None:
        """Stop the preview playback (Batch 4)."""
        stop_playback(self._fallback_player)

    # -- Saving -------------------------------------------------------------

    # Names Windows reserves as devices -- a file literally called
    # "con.wav" or "nul.wav" can't be created normally on Windows.
    _RESERVED_NAMES = {"CON", "PRN", "AUX", "NUL",
                       *(f"COM{i}" for i in range(1, 10)),
                       *(f"LPT{i}" for i in range(1, 10))}

    def _clean_name(self, raw: str) -> str:
        """Turn user input into a safe file stem (no folders / extension).

        This is a security boundary, not just tidiness: input such as
        "../../hack" must resolve to a plain name *inside* ./sounds/,
        never to a path outside it. Path(...).name drops the folders,
        and stripping "." / "/" / "\\" removes anything left over.
        """
        name = raw.strip()
        if name.lower().endswith(".wav"):
            name = name[:-4]
        # Keep it to a single file name: strip any path parts, then
        # remove dots and separators explicitly (defence in depth --
        # Path().name behaves differently for "\\" on POSIX vs Windows).
        name = (
            Path(name).name.replace(" ", "_").replace(".", "")
            .replace("/", "").replace("\\", "")
        )
        # Characters Windows forbids in file names outright. Without
        # this, a name like "a<b" passes the checks above, then saving
        # fails with an unhandled OSError.
        for char in '<>:"|?*':
            name = name.replace(char, "_")
        # Windows also rejects trailing dots/spaces and very long names.
        name = name.strip(" ._")[:60]
        if name.upper() in self._RESERVED_NAMES:
            name = f"_{name}"
        return name

    def on_save(self) -> None:
        """Move the temp preview file to ./sounds/<name>.wav."""
        if self.temp_path is None or not self.temp_path.exists():
            QMessageBox.warning(self, "Nothing to save",
                                "Generate a sound first, then save it.")
            return

        name = self._clean_name(self.name_input.text())
        if not name:
            QMessageBox.warning(self, "Invalid name",
                                "Please enter a name for the sound.")
            return

        destination = self.sounds_dir / f"{name}.wav"
        # Final safeguard, independent of _clean_name: the file we are
        # about to write really must live directly inside the sounds folder.
        if destination.parent.resolve() != self.sounds_dir.resolve():
            QMessageBox.warning(self, "Invalid name",
                                "That name would save outside the sounds folder.")
            return

        if destination.exists():
            answer = QMessageBox.question(
                self, "Overwrite?",
                f"'{destination.name}' already exists. Overwrite it?",
            )
            if answer != QMessageBox.StandardButton.Yes:
                return

        # The preview may still be playing -- stop it before moving the
        # file out from under winsound.
        stop_playback(self._fallback_player)

        try:
            # Path.replace() = move (and it overwrites on all platforms),
            # BUT it only works within one filesystem. TEMP may be on
            # C: while the app lives on D:, which raises OSError
            # (WinError 17) -- so fall back to copy-then-delete.
            try:
                self.temp_path.replace(destination)
            except OSError:
                destination.write_bytes(self.temp_path.read_bytes())
                self.temp_path.unlink()
        except OSError as exc:
            # Leave self.temp_path alone on failure so the user can
            # fix the problem and click Save again instead of losing
            # a sound they liked.
            QMessageBox.warning(self, "Save failed",
                                f"Could not save '{destination.name}':\n{exc}")
            return

        self.temp_path = None
        self.save_button.setEnabled(False)
        self.preview_play_btn.setEnabled(False)
        self.preview_stop_btn.setEnabled(False)
        self.style_label.setText(f"Saved as {destination.name}")

        # Fresh default name for the next sound, then refresh + select it.
        self.name_input.setText(f"custom_{random.randint(1000, 9999)}")
        self.refresh_list(select_name=destination.name)

    # -- Saved-sounds list ----------------------------------------------------

    def refresh_list(self, select_name: str | None = None) -> None:
        """Reload the list widget from ./sounds/."""
        self.sounds_list.clear()
        for wav_path in sorted(self.sounds_dir.glob("*.wav")):
            self.sounds_list.addItem(wav_path.name)
            if wav_path.name == select_name:
                self.sounds_list.setCurrentRow(self.sounds_list.count() - 1)

    def _on_selection_changed(self, row: int) -> None:
        """Enable Play/Delete only when a sound is actually selected."""
        has_selection = row >= 0
        self.play_button.setEnabled(has_selection)
        self.delete_button.setEnabled(has_selection)

    def _selected_path(self) -> Path | None:
        item = self.sounds_list.currentItem()
        return self.sounds_dir / item.text() if item else None

    def on_play(self) -> None:
        """Play the selected saved sound (async) and preview its waveform."""
        path = self._selected_path()
        if path is None or not path.exists():
            return
        self.waveform.load_wav(path)
        self.style_label.setText(f"Playing: {path.name}")
        play_wav_async(path, self._fallback_player)

    def on_delete(self) -> None:
        """Delete the selected saved sound after confirmation."""
        path = self._selected_path()
        if path is None or not path.exists():
            return
        answer = QMessageBox.question(
            self, "Delete sound?", f"Delete '{path.name}' permanently?"
        )
        if answer == QMessageBox.StandardButton.Yes:
            # Deleting the file winsound is currently playing can fail
            # on Windows, so stop playback first.
            stop_playback(self._fallback_player)
            try:
                path.unlink()
            except OSError as exc:
                QMessageBox.warning(self, "Delete failed",
                                    f"Could not delete '{path.name}':\n{exc}")
                return
            self.refresh_list()

    # -- Window lifecycle ---------------------------------------------------

    def closeEvent(self, event) -> None:  # noqa: N802 - Qt naming
        """Stop playback and remove any unsaved preview on close.

        The temp file now lives in the OS temp folder, so even without
        this it wouldn't pollute the app folder -- but deleting it
        ourselves means no junk is left behind at all.
        """
        stop_playback(self._fallback_player)
        if self.temp_path is not None:
            try:
                self.temp_path.unlink(missing_ok=True)
            except OSError:
                pass
        super().closeEvent(event)


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Procedural engine: 100 style profiles, 3 options at a time (numpy)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Every sound is built from scratch in code (sine / square / pulse / saw /
# triangle / FM / Karplus-Strong string / filtered noise), shaped by an
# envelope and an effects chain. There is no sample playback anywhere.
#
# A style is plain data (see S() and L() below). The renderer turns one style
# plus a length in seconds into a float32 mono buffer:
#   fit "tail": the notes play once; for a longer length the voices ring out
#               longer (slower decay) and the reverb tail grows with it.
#   fit "loop": the pattern repeats, fading, until the length is filled.
#   fit "hold": one evolving sustained voice that spans the whole length.
# A length shorter than the pattern compresses the pattern instead.
try:
    import numpy as np
except ImportError:  # the Sounds tab says so and keeps Generate disabled
    np = None

LENGTHS = ((1, "1 second"), (3, "3 seconds"), (5, "5 seconds"), (10, "10 seconds"))
DEFAULT_LENGTH = 3
LEVEL_PEAK = 0.85       # final peak
LEVEL_RMS = 0.12        # quiet styles (hiss, wind) are lifted toward this


def numpy_ok() -> bool:
    """True when numpy is importable. Re-checks, so an install made while the
    app is running (the dialog's Install numpy button) takes effect at once."""
    global np
    if np is None:
        try:
            importlib.invalidate_caches()
            np = importlib.import_module("numpy")
        except Exception:
            return False
    return True


def numpy_install_command() -> list:
    """pip for the exact Python that is running this app."""
    return [sys.executable, "-m", "pip", "install", "numpy>=1.26"]


def _hz(midi: float) -> float:
    return 440.0 * 2.0 ** ((midi - 69.0) / 12.0)


def L(w="sin", **kw):
    """One synth layer. w: sin sq saw tri fm ks noise. Keys: o (octaves),
    st (semitones), len, d (decay /s), a (attack s), r (release s), amp,
    sw (end/start pitch ratio), vib (rate, depth), det (cents), pw (pulse
    width), harm ((mult, amp), ...), fm (ratio, index, index decay), band
    (lo, hi Hz) for noise, ev (only these event numbers), bed (one layer
    spanning the whole length), shape (hump riser fall flat), af / rf
    (attack / release as a fraction of the length, for hold and bed)."""
    d = dict(w=w, o=0, st=0, len=0.4, d=6.0, a=0.003, r=0.01, amp=1.0)
    d.update(kw)
    return d


def S(cat, name, layers, notes=(0,), step=0.0, root=72, fit="tail", fx=(), **kw):
    """One style profile. step 0 = chord (tiny strum); times = explicit event
    times; rand = {'rate', 'n0'} scatters events at random; stretch False
    keeps voices short and lets the reverb fill a longer length."""
    s = dict(cat=cat, name=name, layers=list(layers), notes=notes, step=step,
             root=root, fit=fit, fx=list(fx))
    s.update(kw)
    return s
